messages:
anya (support): FYI - multiple customers reporting 502/504s and request timeouts to hosted inference since ~14:02 PT. Primary signal: gateway errors on generation API. Sample req id: req_8fa2b3. Trying to collect more details.

customer-ops: hitting this now. We have a high priority customer (acct: acme-inc) that saw ~30% request failures, started 14:00. They pasted this error: "UpstreamError: failed to fetch cached KV: timeout after 200ms -> 502". They sent curl repro, attaching below.

anya (support): repro curl from customer:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-...' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-instruct-1","input":"Summarize X"}' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: req_8fa2b3'
```
Response: 502 with body: `\{"error\":{\"type\":\"upstream_error\",\"message\":\"KV fetch timeout\"}}`

dan (eng-oncall): I see a spike in 5xx and origin latencies across the serving fleet at 14:00. Paging infra. Primary symptom appears to be KV/prefix cache calls timing out -> blocking generate path. Can someone grab redis/memcached metrics for prefix cache cluster?

infra-bot: Alert: redis-cache-prod cluster high p99 latency and connection errors. Epoch: 2026-03-15T21:04:02Z. Observed: increased cmd latency >500ms, timeout errors, client_rejected connections. Pager: oncall@infra.

alex (runtime): Thanks. From runtime logs for node rrt-17 during spike:
```
[14:03:14] req=req_8fa2b3 INFO fetching prefix keys for model=rwd-instruct-1
[14:03:14] req=req_8fa2b3 WARN KVFetchTimeout: waited 250ms for redis GET -> raising error (KVFetchTimeout)
[14:03:14] req=req_8fa2b3 ERROR upstream gateway returned 502: KV fetch failed
```
We don't currently have a circuit-breaker around cache; runtime bails with 5xx when KV fetch fails in some code paths (should probably fallback to cold path but doesn't for certain prefetch code).

maya (sre): Can we flip the runtime flag to disable prefix caching for production temporarily? That will route requests to cold path, higher latency but should reduce 5xxs. Also let's add a short-term retry/backoff for KV fetch.

alex (runtime): I can push a hotfix to enable `prefix_cache.enabled=false` via remote config. Patch ready, need PRD approval to run on prod. Patch mitigations:
- disable prefix/prefetch cache (config flip)
- add 1st-order retry (50ms) for KV GET
- increase KV timeout from 200ms -> 500ms while infra stabilizes

dan (eng-oncall): Do it. Post an update to customers. Please run the change on a single region first and measure.

deploy-bot: Starting rollout: config-change prefix_cache.enabled=false -> targeting region us-west-2 (canary 10%)

alex (runtime): canary applied at 14:22. Error rate drop on canary nodes immediately visible: 5xx rate down from 18% -> 1.4% for canary traffic. Rolling to 100% now.

infra-bot: Redis cluster (redis-cache-prod) reporting OOM eviction spikes and backlog of pending commands. Observed TTL churn and high eviction rates across several shards.

maya (sre): Infra, what's root cause? Eviction churn suggests memory pressure possibly due to a bug in prefix key TTLs or an external batch job loading many keys.

infra-bot: We detected an automated job from analytics-team that warmed prefix keys at 13:56 and attempted bulk writes (~2.1M keys) without TTLs. That, combined with normal traffic, exhausted memory -> eviction -> latency and timeouts.

infra-bot: Action taken: stopped the job and scaled redis-cache-prod by +2 nodes; restarted sentinels. New nodes are rebalancing.

alex (runtime): Rolling config rollback not needed; cold path fallback kept disabled for now because canary shows stability. Latency avg increased ~30-40ms but 5xxs down to baseline. Logs show KV timeouts gone for most requests.

anya (support): Customer update sent: "we identified a transient cache service issue causing timeouts; we've mitigated by disabling the prefix cache and scaling the cache cluster. Your traffic should be healthy now; please ping if you still see failures." :white_check_mark:

liz (product): Need a postmortem and customer-facing blurb. Also we should confirm if any customer data was affected (unlikely but verify audit logs).

dan (eng-oncall): Immediate next actions (short list):
- infra: confirm redis eviction root cause and add quota/safeguards to prevent uncontrolled warm jobs
- runtime: add circuit-breaker + fallback for prefetch code path (ticket RT-4289)
- runtime: implement retriable KV GET (with jitter/backoff) and expose config thresholds
- product/support: follow up with affected customers and offer incident summary

maya (sre): I'll file INC-2026-042 and schedule a postmortem. Tentative severity P2 given customer impact on multi-tenant hosted API. Link: https://incidents.internal/inc/INC-2026-042

alex (runtime): Temporary mitigations committed:
- prefix_cache.enabled=false (prod)
- KV timeout = 500ms
- 1 retry added to KV GET
Will follow up with PRs to make circuit-breaker permanent.

anya (support): Customer confirmed recovery at 14:48 PT. They saw generation succeed and error rate cleared.

maya (sre): Monitoring/alerts to add:
- alert when redis client_rejected > 0
- alert when eviction rate spikes above 0.1% per min
- add a synthetic test that hits prefix cache paths and asserts 95th latency < 80ms

dan (eng-oncall): Good. Copy of quick repro steps for support/escalations (put in runbook):
1) curl with X-Request-ID -> collect req id
2) collect runtime logs for that req id (node id in header)
3) check redis-cache-prod metrics (p99 cmd latency, client_rejected, evictions)
4) if KVFetchTimeout seen, toggle `prefix_cache.enabled=false` via remote config and monitor
5) scale cache or kill offending warm jobs

anya (support): Closing thread after incident follow-up. Will attach customer communications to INC-2026-042. Thanks everyone. :pray:
